question: Why does an onigiri wrapper keep the seaweed behind a plastic film?
angle: The inner film keeps moist rice and crisp seaweed apart until you open it; the numbered tabs (1, 2, 3) are the order to remove the film so the seaweed wraps the rice. Date line must be exact: Seven-Eleven Japan launched packaged onigiri in 1978. The opening (and closing) image must be a real triangular konbini onigiri in its clear wrapper, seaweed sheet visible behind the film. Tab images must show the whole triangular wrapper front-on: top pull strip and both bottom corner flaps. Witty angle: soggy seaweed is everyone's sad lunch. Ending: the second-to-last line gives the answer, the last line is a lead-in such as 'So next time someone asks you...' that flows straight into the opening question.
